codes.meaning: The scene carries a non-finite or negative extent, so nothing can be rasterized.
codes.trigger: A rect, radius, or stroke width is NaN, infinite, or negative when a scene node is built.
codes.span: No authored text exists at scene construction, so the host reports the failing node.

codes.meaning: A style value is outside the range the scene model accepts.
codes.trigger: An opacity outside 0..=1 or a font size at or below zero.
codes.span: No authored text exists at scene construction, so the host reports the failing node.

codes.meaning: A transform component is not finite.
codes.trigger: A translate, scale, rotate, or skew component is NaN or infinite.
codes.span: No authored text exists at scene construction, so the host reports the failing node.

codes.meaning: A complete scene could not be written to its vector output.
codes.trigger: An id or attribute collides after escaping, or an element the serializer cannot express.
codes.span: No authored text exists at serialization, so the host reports the failing element.

codes.meaning: The frontend rejected the fence before it could hand back a tree.
codes.trigger: An Oak parser returns a hard error instead of a recovered tree, which the DOT, Mermaid, and PlantUML parsers only do for input they cannot even tokenize.
codes.span: The parser reports no location today, so every entry falls back to the whole fence body.

codes.meaning: The frontend ran but produced no AST the lowering can walk.
codes.trigger: An Oak frontend returns an empty or unusable document tree.
codes.span: The whole fence body, because there is no construct to name.

codes.meaning: The source parsed, but this family or construct has no lowering into a DaVinci scene.
codes.trigger: A Mermaid family outside flowchart, sequence, class, or state, a second diagram header, an illegal orientation, a sequence block or note that would be dropped, a DOT HTML-like label, record shape, named port, `pos`, `splines`, `URL`, or a second graph, a PlantUML `skinparam`, missing terminator, or missing header.
codes.span: The rejected statement or attribute when the frontend can point at it, otherwise the whole fence body.

codes.meaning: A construct is drawn with a different scene primitive than the one it names.
codes.trigger: A DOT node shape or arrowhead with no exact primitive, which is drawn as box or plain line.
codes.span: The attribute that names the approximated shape or arrowhead.

codes.meaning: The fence declares a diagram with nothing to draw.
codes.trigger: A DOT or Mermaid body with no nodes and no edges.

codes.meaning: The chart has no rows or no columns to encode.
codes.trigger: An empty `values` array, or an encoding that selects no field.

codes.meaning: Two columns disagree on how many rows the snapshot holds.
codes.trigger: Inline rows with different key counts after projection.

codes.meaning: A value cannot be read as the kind its field declares.
codes.trigger: A string in a quantitative field, or an object in a nominal field.

codes.meaning: A row has no value for a field the encoding needs, so that row is skipped.
codes.trigger: A row that omits an encoded field or carries `null` for it, which leaves the affected rows out of the marks.
codes.span: The row object inside `data.values`, otherwise the column that owns the skipped rows.

codes.meaning: A quantitative value is NaN or infinite.
codes.trigger: A literal `null` accepted as numeric, or a value the reader cannot keep finite.

codes.meaning: Two columns or two channel bindings share one field name.
codes.trigger: The same field bound twice, or duplicate keys in one row.
codes.span: The `encoding` node that repeats the field.

codes.meaning: An encoding points at a field the data does not carry.
codes.trigger: A `field` value absent from every row.
codes.span: The binding object that names the field.

codes.meaning: The specification parses but contradicts itself.
codes.trigger: A non-boolean `zero` or `nice`, a non-string title, a width or height that is not a number.
codes.span: The smallest JSON node that carries the contradiction.

codes.meaning: A scale declaration cannot be trained on the values its channel holds.
codes.trigger: Zero or negative values under `log` or `sqrt`, or an empty domain.

codes.meaning: A channel has no values to train its scale.
codes.trigger: Every row missing the encoded field.
codes.span: The binding object of the channel.

codes.meaning: A domain collapsed to one value and was expanded to stay drawable.
codes.trigger: Every value identical, or a zero-width quantitative range.

codes.meaning: A mark or guide is drawn approximately, or not at all.
codes.trigger: A tick label that cannot fit, or a mark the author asked for but the plan drops.
codes.span: The `encoding` node that owns the approximated mark.

codes.meaning: The authored fence is not valid JSON.
codes.trigger: A syntax error, or trailing content after the document.
codes.span: The failing byte range the JSON reader reports, otherwise the whole fence body.

codes.meaning: The document carries a key outside the accepted subset.
codes.trigger: A top-level, `encoding`, `mark`, `scale`, or `data` key the subset does not name.

codes.meaning: The document declares a mark outside the accepted subset.
codes.trigger: `rule`, `arc`, `area`, `tick`, `point`, or an object mark with an unaccepted type.

codes.meaning: The document binds a channel outside the accepted subset.
codes.trigger: A `shape`, `size`, `row`, `column`, `theta`, or `detail` binding.

codes.meaning: A channel key or statistic is outside the accepted subset.
codes.trigger: An aggregate or scale key the subset does not implement.

codes.meaning: The document declares a scale outside the accepted subset.
codes.trigger: `pow`, `symlog`, `quantile`, or a scale with an unaccepted domain or range form.

codes.meaning: The document declares a data transform.
codes.trigger: Any `transform` array, including `filter`, `calculate`, and `timeUnit`.

codes.meaning: The document declares a composed view.
codes.trigger: `layer`, `hconcat`, `vconcat`, `concat`, `facet`, or `repeat`.

codes.meaning: The document declares interaction or selection state.
codes.trigger: `params`, `selection`, or `bind` on a mark.

codes.meaning: The document points at data that is not inline.
codes.trigger: `data.url`, `data.name`, or a dataset outside `data.values`.

matrix.reason: `REJECTIONS` in `every_rejection_is_structured_and_named_with_a_json_path` already authors `$.data.url`, a fence fixture would assert the same bytes
the refusal branch is a closed key list with no data dependency, already authored inline in `REJECTIONS` for `$.encoding.x.axis`, and a fence fixture would repeat identical bytes
cross-channel conflict is asserted inline by `a_bin_channel_that_is_also_an_aggregate_is_refused_by_the_spec`, which owns the exact code and path
every invalid combination is enumerated by `unsupported_bin_options_are_refused_before_any_scene_is_built`, one fixture per combination would be redundant
the refusal is authored on the data side with no JSON path, and `a_value_below_the_declared_extent_is_refused_instead_of_clamped` already pins the code and the body span
`unlisted_time_units_and_local_prefixes_are_refused_with_a_path` already covers both spellings with the JSON path
the branch is a closed token list with no data dependency, and `REJECTIONS` already exercises the same code for the non-linear options
`REJECTIONS` authors `$.encoding.y.scale.zero` on a `log` scale inline
`REJECTIONS` authors the `zero` plus `domain` conflict and `a_log_scale_places_decades_evenly_and_rejects_non_positive_values` covers the non-positive domain
`REJECTIONS` authors `$.layer` inline and every other key shares the same branch
`REJECTIONS` authors `$.params` inline

matrix.item: legend guides and untrainable axis guides

matrix.reason: this row buckets seven column validation codes that the compile and snapshot suites cover per code, a fixture would pin only one of them

matrix.item: fence body that is not JSON
matrix.reason: `invalid_json_reports_the_position_of_the_failure` pins the one-byte span, and serde error positions change with the parser version so a frozen fixture would rot
the span is the whole header line, byte-identical to `diagram-mermaid-second-header`, so a second fixture would assert the same range
all five bracket spellings are refused at their own lines by `unsupported_flowchart_shapes_are_refused_at_their_line`, one fixture per spelling would be redundant
eight statements are refused by `flowchart_dropped_statements_are_refused_at_their_line`, which owns the exact per-statement span
fourteen statements are refused by `class_dropped_statements_are_refused_at_their_line`, which also proves the member body is skipped
`flowchart_without_nodes_reports_empty_diagram` pins the body span, and the fixture would need an otherwise complete diagram
the branch needs a byte sequence the Oak frontend refuses while the header stays valid, which an authored fixture cannot keep stable across frontend revisions

matrix.item: parseable Mermaid without an Oak AST
matrix.reason: the branch needs a successful parse that returns no AST, a state authored bytes cannot force
the span is the rankdir value, the same range row 17 refuses, and the check is a closed token list

matrix.item: named ports, subgraph operands, anonymous subgraphs, nested clusters, non-`rank=same` subgraphs
matrix.reason: five structural forms are refused by `nested_clusters_and_rankless_subgraphs_are_rejected`, one fixture per form would repeat the same branch
eighteen keys share one whitelist check, and `layout_and_interaction_attributes_are_rejected_with_their_spans` already asserts the per-attribute span
`multiple_graphs_are_rejected_at_the_second_graph` and `strict_graphs_unknown_styles_and_mismatched_edge_operators_are_rejected` cover both spellings
the branch needs a malformed token stream the Oak frontend rejects, which an authored fixture cannot keep stable across frontend revisions

matrix.item: missing or repeated markers, content outside markers, `!include`, foreign start markers

matrix.reason: seventeen families share one refusal branch in `statements_outside_the_class_and_sequence_subset_are_refused`

matrix.item: class and sequence mixed in one PlantUML source
matrix.reason: `mixed_class_and_sequence_sources_are_refused_at_the_contradicting_marker` pins the contradicting marker span

matrix.item: self edges (DOT `a -> a`, Mermaid `A->>A`, PlantUML self message)
matrix.reason: neither the layered layout nor the time-ordered layout has a loop route, so the edge is skipped with an error located on its own statement and the rest of the scene still renders. `a_self_edge_is_refused_at_its_own_statement` pins the DOT case

matrix.item: four-corner and centre DOT compass ports

matrix.reason: `a_cycle_reports_the_back_edge_and_its_authored_span` pins the DOT label, span = the edge statement that no longer advances to a later layer (`b -> a`), and the message names every reversed edge. The layout still routes every edge, so the row has no rejection fixture

DOT, Mermaid and PlantUML all create an implicit node for an unknown endpoint, so authored source never reaches this branch. It fires only for a hand-built `DiagramSpec`, which carries no token, and `an_edge_to_an_undeclared_node_is_refused_at_its_statement` covers it

matrix.item: duplicate id (node, cluster, or sequence participant)
matrix.reason: `a_duplicate_participant_is_reported_at_its_second_declaration` pins the PlantUML label, span = the second declaration statement (`participant Alice`). Node and cluster ids are deduplicated by every frontend, so those two keep the same hand-built guard as `an_edge_to_an_undeclared_node_is_refused_at_its_statement`

an unknown port keeps the route and falls back to the default anchor for the layout direction. DOT refuses named ports before lowering and registers every compass port, so only a hand-built `DiagramSpec` reaches the fallback, covered by `an_edge_to_an_undeclared_port_keeps_its_route_on_the_default_anchor`
